vibe.title: Vibe Check
vibe.content:
SLOW JAM: MARIAH CAREY, "HERO" (1993)
• No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 for four weeks, Christmas Day 1993 into January 1994.
• Mariah wrote it with Walter Afanasieff; it was first meant for Gloria Estefan and the movie Hero before Tommy Mottola convinced Mariah to keep it.
• Why today: it's game week for two area teams, and a soft song about finding the strength inside is the right way to wake up a town that's about to drive to Clare.
😂 JOKES: Every Stags parent is going to sing this in the bleachers Saturday. Off-key. Proudly. / Mariah almost gave this song away. That's like Kingsley giving away the Wing-T playbook.

🚗 DRIVE TEASE: Dry roads and clear skies early, about 41 at 6 AM with calm winds; sunny then clouds by midday, up to 62 this afternoon.

📅 THIS DAY: "THE BAND IS OUT ON THE FIELD!" (NOV. 20, 1982)
• Forty-four years ago today, Cal and Stanford played the Big Game. Stanford, with John Elway, kicked a field goal to lead 20-19 with four seconds left.
• On the kickoff, Cal threw five laterals while the Stanford band, thinking the game was over, marched onto the field.
• Cal's Kevin Moen ran through the band and scored, 25-20 Cal. KGO's Joe Starkey's call, "The band is out on the field!", is one of the most famous in sports.
😂 JOKES: The Stanford trombone player is still telling people he 'almost made the tackle.' / Moral of the story: never leave a football game early. Or a band practice.

💡 FUN FACT: GTA 6 VS. THE BOX OFFICE
• GTA 6's estimated $2.36 billion from pre-orders and day one is almost as much as the year's top movie, Spider-Man: Brand New Day, made in its entire theater run ($2.5 billion), per the BBC.
😂 JOKES: One day of GTA 6 nearly equals a whole summer of Spider-Man. Spidey's going to need a second job. / Movie theaters are offering free refills now. Rockstar's offering free sleep deprivation.

🎉 NATIONAL DAYS: National Absurdity Day · National Peanut Butter Fudge Day · National Child's Day · Substitute Educators Day

GOOD MORNING UP NORTH: 41 and clear at drive time, sunny turning cloudy midday, high 62. A breezy, mild night tonight at 52 with south gusts to 30. Small Craft Advisory on the Bay and Lake Michigan from this afternoon through late Saturday night (Bay waves 2-3 ft tonight, Lake MI 3-5 ft).

SCHOOLS: No closings or delays listed this morning.

ROADS: Dry. Saturday 3-8 PM Front Street closes Franklin to Pine for the Light Parade.

ENERGY: Game weekend. Stags Saturday, Snowbirds Saturday, Roscommon at noon today, and the tree lights up tonight.

MOOD BOOST: SMASH MOUTH, "ALL STAR" (1999)
• Peaked at No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100 in August 1999.
• Guitarist Greg Camp wrote it late in the Astro Lounge sessions when the label asked for more singles, and he set out to write an anthem for outcasts, drawing on Sugar Ray and Third Eye Blind.
• Why today: 'Hey now, you're an all star' for every Stag, Snowbird and Roscommon volleyball player playing this weekend.
😂 JOKES: This song has been in Shrek, every 2000s roller rink, and every dad's car. It's earned its place. / Somebody, once, told me the Stags were going to Ford Field. I believed them.

buzz.title: Daily Buzz
buzz.content:
━━ LOCAL ━━

STAG IT UP: KINGSLEY VS. ALMONT, THE REMATCH
• SUMMARY: Kingsley (12-0) and Almont (12-0) meet tomorrow, Saturday, Nov. 21, at 1 PM in the Division 6 state semifinal at the Brookwood Athletic Complex in Clare. Winner goes to Ford Field for the D6 final, Friday, Nov. 27, at 4 PM.
• HOW WE GOT HERE: Last Friday the Stags beat Sanford Meridian 34-28 in a battle of unbeatens for the regional title. QB Barrett Bielas after the win: "Anything for one more week."
• THE CATCH: It's a rematch. Kingsley beat Almont 38-24 for the 2023 D6 state title at Ford Field, and Almont has been a semifinal regular since (45-4 the last four years).
• WHO: Stags RB Perry Smith (1,260 yards, 19 TDs), Nolan Hodges (828 yards, 15 TDs), Eric Stark (591, 8 TDs), WR Andrew George (292 receiving, 3 TDs). Almont's Brody Corneau ran for 111 yards on 12 carries last week.
• WHAT: Two mirror images. Kingsley averages about 41 points and allows 15; Almont averages 40 and allows 16.5.
• WHERE/HOW: Tickets are $12 on GoFan. Streaming on the NFHS Network.
• WHY IT MATTERS: Kingsley lost the 2025 final to Lumen Christi 28-14. One more win and the Stags are back at Ford Field for a second straight year.
➜ TAKE: Two undefeated teams, one ticket to Ford Field. This is a two-hour drive and a lifetime memory. Wear your Stags gear, bring a blanket, and yell till Sunday.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: your Stags score prediction, and who's driving down to Clare?
😂 JOKES: Almont's coming in 12-0. That's cute. So is Kingsley. Somebody's about to find out what 12-1 feels like. / If you see a long line of Stags flags on US-127 Saturday morning, that's not traffic. That's a parade with a GPS.

LIGHT UP DOWNTOWN: NIGHT ONE IS TONIGHT
• Traverse City's holiday kickoff is two nights for the first time. Tonight (Friday) is the tree lighting; the Light Parade is Saturday at 6 PM.
• Tonight from 4 to 6:30 PM: a cookies-and-cocoa crawl, a Find the Grinch scavenger hunt, carolers and vendors, plus a variety show at 5 PM. Santa lights the 4,500-pound blue spruce at Cass and Front at 6:30.
• The DDA's Sara Klebba says they split it up to manage the crowds and make it safer and more comfortable.
• Heads-up for Saturday: Front Street closes Franklin to Pine from 3 to 8 PM, and cars parked in the closure get towed to Thirlby Field.
➜ TAKE: Two nights of Christmas downtown. Finally, a way to see the parade without standing behind a guy who's seven feet tall.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: tree lighting tonight or parade tomorrow? Which one is your family doing?
😂 JOKES: Find the Grinch scavenger hunt. Easy. He's the guy complaining about parking. / A 4,500-pound tree in a manhole. That's the most Traverse City sentence ever written.

ONE AUTHOR'S POST, PHONES RINGING ON FRONT STREET
• Horizon Books in downtown TC is getting orders from all over the country for signed books.
• New York Times bestselling romance author Abby Jimenez has a daughter at Interlochen Arts Academy. When she's in town she signs stacks at Horizon and posts about it.
• COO Juan Pineda says the phones start ringing right after, and signed copies have shipped as far as Texas and California. It's moving her backlist too.
➜ TAKE: One social post and a local bookstore turns into a national mail-order business. That's the most romantic plot twist in a romance-novel story.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: what's the one book you'd drive across the country for a signed copy of?
😂 JOKES: Horizon Books is now shipping to Texas. Next up, a drive-thru window for book clubs. / Nothing says love story like a woman, a Sharpie and a bookstore phone that won't stop ringing.

GAYLORD WAVES THE SNOWBIRDS OFF TO MARQUETTE
• Gaylord St. Mary is in its first state football final since 2002: the 8-player Division 2 title game vs. Mendon, Saturday at 2 PM in the Superior Dome in Marquette.
• The school held a pep rally Thursday. This morning the team bus leaves at 10 AM, and the town is invited to line Petoskey and Main streets to wave them off.
• Coach Kevin O'Connell: "For such a small community, you realize how big it actually is."
➜ TAKE: Nothing beats a small town lining Main Street for a school bus. Honk twice if you're stuck behind it. Honk proud.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: shout out a Snowbird or a Stag, we'll read it on air.
😂 JOKES: The Snowbirds are heading north for the winter. That's the opposite of how snowbirds work. / Superior Dome. Even the stadium name is trash-talking.

DEER SEASON FASHION: ORANGE VESTS FOR THE DOG
• Alden Canvas, a family canvas shop near Rapid City in Kalkaska County, makes blaze-style safety vests for dogs so they stay visible on walks.
• The vests are free; they only ask for a donation, and every dollar goes to Antrim County Animal Control.
• So far 164 vests are out and about $680 has been donated. Owner Chris Dewald says demand got a lot bigger this year, and they want photos of the pups wearing them.
➜ TAKE: It's deer season. If the dog's out in the woods, the dog wears orange. Fashion and safety, and the shelter gets the money.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: send us your dog's name and its most ridiculous outfit.
😂 JOKES: My dog in a safety vest looks like he's about to direct traffic at the Cherry Festival. / Free vest for the dog. Meanwhile, I'm still paying full price for my own hat.

━━ NATIONAL ━━

DUA LIPA, LANA AND CAMILA ON THE GTA 6 ALBUM, OUT TODAY
• Rockstar released Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album today, Nov. 20: 34 songs, a day after the game came out.
• New tracks include Dua Lipa's "Go Easy," Lana Del Rey's "Crazy for You," Camila Cabello's "Sweet Like Candy" and Zara Larsson's "Fast Emotion."
• It also has Morgan Wallen, Travis Scott, JENNIE and Justice with Tame Impala and SZA. The tracklist leaked early when vinyl copies showed up at a store.
➜ TAKE: The biggest video game ever just turned into a pop album. Somewhere a teenager is saying 'I only play it for the soundtrack.'
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: what song would be on the soundtrack of YOUR life?
😂 JOKES: Dua Lipa's new song is called 'Go Easy.' Nobody playing GTA has ever gone easy. / Morgan Wallen and Dua Lipa on one album. That's the most Up North playlist I've ever seen.

THE HUNGER GAMES ARE BACK, AND THE ODDS LOOK GOOD
• The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping opens today in about 3,900 theaters. It's the sixth movie in the series.
• Thursday previews brought in more than $21 million, the franchise's second-best preview night ever (Deadline).
• Lionsgate is projecting about $85 million for the weekend, but theater owners think it could get close to $125 million. The last one, Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes, opened at $44 million.
➜ TAKE: Friday movie night just got serious. Bring snacks. Bring tissues. Do NOT volunteer as tribute for the popcorn run.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: what's the one skill you'd bring to the Hunger Games? Be honest. Mine is napping.
😂 JOKES: May the odds be ever in your favor. And may the person in front of you not be on their phone. / I'd last about four minutes in the Hunger Games. Three if there's no Wi-Fi.

━━ BITS ━━

NATIONAL ABSURDITY DAY: THE WEIRDEST RULE IN YOUR HOUSE
• Today is National Absurdity Day, a day for the totally off-the-wall stuff.
• Example from National Day Calendar: when parcel post started in 1913, some kids were literally mailed to Grandma's house, some for as little as 15 cents plus insurance.
• So today: what's the most absurd rule in your house? No shoes upstairs? Nobody touches Dad's thermostat? The dog gets the good couch?
➜ TAKE: Every house has one rule that makes zero sense to company. Ours is: nobody eats the last pickle. Nobody. It's just there, living its life.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: the most absurd rule in your house.
😂 JOKES: Mailing a kid for 15 cents? I'd pay that just for a quiet ride to school. / Absurdity Day in Michigan is called 'wearing shorts in November,' and we did it all week.

PREDICT THE STAGS SCORE
• Kingsley vs. Almont, Saturday 1 PM in Clare. Two 12-0 teams. Winner goes to Ford Field.
• Call or text your final score. Closest guess gets bragging rights on Monday's show.
➜ TAKE: I'm not saying I'll be right, but I'm saying I've already practiced my Monday victory voice.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: your final score, Stags vs. Almont.
😂 JOKES: If you predict Almont wins, please text from an unlisted number for your own safety. / Last time these two met it was 38-24. I'm predicting a score with a lot of numbers in it.

━━ SPORTS ━━

KINGSLEY: D6 SEMIFINAL SATURDAY
Kingsley (12-0) vs. Almont (12-0) · Sat 1 PM · Brookwood Athletic Complex, Clare · $12 GoFan · NFHS Network stream.
Rundown: Stags beat Meridian 34-28 in the regional; Perry Smith has 1,260 yards and 19 TDs. Winner plays the D6 final at Ford Field, Fri Nov 27, 4 PM.

GAYLORD ST. MARY: 8-PLAYER D2 FINAL SATURDAY
Gaylord St. Mary vs. Mendon · Sat 2 PM · Superior Dome, Marquette. Team bus leaves Gaylord 10 AM today, send-off on Petoskey and Main.
Rundown: first title game for the Snowbirds since 2002; they won the semi 39-36.

ROSCOMMON VOLLEYBALL: D3 STATE SEMI TODAY
Roscommon vs. Kalamazoo Christian · today NOON · Kellogg Arena, Battle Creek. D3 final is Saturday at Kellogg.

FRIDAY NIGHT HS FOOTBALL
No Grand Traverse–area games tonight. TC Central, TC West, St. Francis, Elk Rapids, Glen Lake, Benzie Central, Suttons Bay, Leland, Buckley and Kalkaska are done for the year; Kingsley is the last area 11-player team standing (Saturday).

MSU TONIGHT: OREGON ON SENIOR NIGHT
Michigan State (3-7) vs. No. 13 Oregon (7-3) · tonight 8:05 PM · Spartan Stadium · FOX.
Rundown: senior night; Oregon won the last meeting 31-10 in 2024.

MICHIGAN SATURDAY: NO. 4 UCLA
Michigan vs. No. 4 UCLA · Sat 3:30 PM · Michigan Stadium · CBS · home finale. Ohio State is next Saturday at noon on FOX.

LIONS SUNDAY: BUCS AT FORD FIELD
Lions (7-2) vs. Tampa Bay · Sun 1 PM · Ford Field · FOX.
Rundown: the Bucs lead the league in interceptions (16) and takeaways (21); the Lions are third in sacks with 32.

DETROIT QUICK HITS
Tigers: three AL Silver Sluggers (Riley Greene, Dillon Dingler, Kevin McGonigle), first time since 1987.
Pistons beat New Orleans 122-109 Wednesday, 17 threes. Red Wings lost 4-1 to Boston on their Centennial night.

• The Old Mission Peninsula Women's Club packed Thanksgiving baskets Thursday for 12 local families, its 33rd year doing it.

localBench.body:
TC VACATION RENTAL CAP HEADS TO A DEC. 7 VOTE
• Traverse City commissioners voted Monday to send new short-term rental limits to a Dec. 7 enactment vote.
• Vacation rentals aren't allowed in neighborhoods but cluster in commercial districts. Since 2021 three districts cap them at 25 percent of units on a property.
• In other districts, 100 percent of units can be vacation rentals right now, and residents asked for tighter rules in the city's strategic plan. The proposal would cut those percentages.
➜ TAKE: Downtown wants neighbors, not just suitcases. December 7 is the vote, so if you've got an opinion, that's the night.

STAGS EXTRAS: KINGSLEY VS. ALMONT
• Kingsley 12-0, Almont 12-0. Somebody's perfect season ends Saturday in Clare.
• Rematch: Kingsley beat Almont 38-24 in the 2023 D6 state final at Ford Field.
• The Stags score about 41 a game and give up 15; Almont scores 40 and gives up 16.5.
• Kingsley has scored 31 or more in six straight games and won seven straight at home.
• Perry Smith: 1,260 rushing yards, 19 TDs. Nolan Hodges: 828 yards, 15 TDs. It's a Wing-T, so everybody gets the ball.
• QB Barrett Bielas after the regional: "Anything for one more week."
• Kingsley has made the playoffs nine straight years and lost the 2025 final to Lumen Christi, 28-14.
• Win and it's Ford Field, Friday Nov. 27 at 4 PM. Tickets for Saturday: $12 on GoFan.
😂 STAGS ONE-LINERS: The Stags run the Wing-T. Almont's defense is about to learn it stands for 'Where'd they go?' / Clare's a two-hour drive. Kingsley fans will make it in an hour fifty with a stop for jerky. / Almont's coming up with 12 wins. Kingsley's bringing 12 wins and a whole town's worth of casseroles.
📞 Call or text 231-929-4487 with your Stags prediction: final score and who scores first.
📞 Shout-out line: Stags players, parents, grandparents, call in and tell us who you're cheering for by name.
🎯 PREDICTION BIT: AJ and the studio each lock a final score at 7:40; read the best listener texts at 8:40; Monday's show crowns the closest guess (bragging rights only).

gta6.title: GTA 6 Watch
gta6.content:
GTA 6 WATCH: DAY TWO
• CONFIRMED: Sensor Tower estimates GTA 6 pre-orders plus first-day sales topped 24.5 million copies and about $2.36 billion. The BBC notes this year's top movie, Spider-Man: Brand New Day, made $2.5 billion in its whole theater run.
• CONFIRMED: Rockstar and Take-Two haven't released official sales numbers; they call demand "unprecedented."
• CONFIRMED: GTA VI: The Album is out today, 34 songs including Dua Lipa, Lana Del Rey, Camila Cabello and Morgan Wallen. A one-off GTA 6 music festival hits Miami Saturday with Travis Scott, Cardi B and more.
• REPORTED, NOT CONFIRMED: no PC version or GTA Online date announced; reports point to 2027.
➜ TAKE: It made almost as much in one day as the biggest movie of the year made all year. My kid's going to use that stat to argue for a later bedtime.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: did anybody in your house actually sleep this week?
😂 JOKES: $2.36 billion in a day. That's a lot of people telling their boss they had 'a family thing.' / GTA 6 has a soundtrack album now. Great, now the car rides AND the video game are loud.

UPDATE 6:00 AM
• Biggest entertainment launch in history (BBC / Sensor Tower): GTA 6 is estimated to be the biggest entertainment launch ever. Niko Partners expects more than $3 billion in sales this year. ON WALL STREET: Take-Two stock jumped 6% on the 99 reviews, and Wells Fargo now expects about 65 million copies sold by March. No stock market record yet; shares actually dipped about 2% on launch day.
• GTA 6 streams break records: 125 million hours watched in 24 hours (CNN / Streams Charts): Streams Charts reports GTA 6 streams racked up 125.47 million hours watched in the first 24 hours, peaking at 7.91 million concurrent viewers across Twitch, YouTube and Kick. The Twitch peak of 3.31 million makes GTA 6 the most-watched game ever on the platform, passing League of Legends' 2022 World Championship final.
• GTA 6 downloads set a world record for internet traffic (ComicBook / DE-CIX): During Wednesday evening's download rush, data flowing through DE-CIX's global internet exchanges hit a record 33.03 terabits per second. DE-CIX says that is about a 25% jump in internet usage compared to the start of the year, driven by millions downloading GTA 6 at the same time.
• GTA 6 sits at 99 on Metacritic, tying the site's highest score ever (FinanceFeeds): GTA 6 holds a 99 on Metacritic across 147 critic reviews, tying the highest rating the site has ever recorded. The score can still drift as more reviews come in.

lifestyle.title: Lifestyle & Trends
lifestyle.content:
GAS IS FALLING, AND TWO-THIRDS OF US ARE DRIVING TO DINNER
• GasBuddy's Thanksgiving survey (Nov 19): 66% of Americans plan a road trip for Thanksgiving, up from 60% last year.
• GasBuddy forecasts a $3.62 national average on Thanksgiving Day, down more than 50 cents in a month but still about 60 cents above last year.
• Nearly one in five drivers (18%) say they're cutting other holiday spending to cover gas.
➜ LOCAL ANGLE: Up North, Thanksgiving is a driving holiday: Grandma's in Gaylord, the cousins in Grand Rapids. Cheaper gas on US-131 and I-75 is real money.
➜ TAKE: Prices are dropping just in time for the drive to Grandma's. Fill up early in the week before everybody else does.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: how far are you driving for Thanksgiving dinner?
😂 JOKES: Two-thirds of us are road-tripping. The other third is hosting and quietly hoping the roads close. / Gas dropped 50 cents. I celebrated by buying 50 cents' worth of gas-station jerky.

THANKSGIVING IS STILL HOMEMADE
• YouGov's new poll (Nov 19): 84% plan to celebrate Thanksgiving, and 78% will do it at their home or a friend's or family member's home.
• 83% say their group will cook the meal; only 5% will order a premade dinner and 4% will go out to eat.
• Turkey, mashed potatoes and pie top the list of what people expect to eat.
➜ LOCAL ANGLE: Up North we cook at home and fight over whose pie it is. Local pie shops are already taking orders for people who'd rather not.
➜ TAKE: Ordering in is out. America still wants to be in the kitchen at 6 AM wrestling a turkey. Respect.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: what's the one dish you're not allowed to skip at your Thanksgiving?
😂 JOKES: 83% cook at home. The other 17% have already been banned from the kitchen. / Pie made the top three. Correct. Pie should be top one, two and three.

officeschool.title: Office & School Bits
officeschool.content:
OFFICE: FEWER OF US GET THANKSGIVING OFF
• YouGov: 58% of working Americans say they get Thanksgiving Day off, down from 68% last year.
• 19% say they'll work full or limited hours on the holiday.
➜ TAKE: If you're working Thursday, you're a hero. And you get first dibs on the leftovers in the break room.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: working Thanksgiving? Tell us where, we'll give you a shout.
😂 JOKES: Working Thanksgiving means you get to skip the family argument. Some people call that a perk. / Somebody's bringing a turkey sandwich to the office Thursday and becoming a legend.

OFFICE: DROVE IN TO SIT ON ZOOM
• A New York Fed survey says about half of office-based workers describe in-office days full of Zoom calls and Slack threads, with little face time with coworkers.
• Reasons include remote teammates, teams spread across the map, and people not actually showing up on mandated days.
➜ TAKE: You scraped the windshield, fought traffic, found a parking spot, and then got on a video call with the guy sitting ten feet away.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: what's the most pointless meeting you've ever been in?
😂 JOKES: I drove 20 minutes to join a Zoom. My laptop could've done that from the couch. / Office life now: you can hear your coworker in the room AND on the call. It's surround sound.

SCHOOL: AN 'EDUCATOR VILLAGE' FOR TEACHERS
• Garfield Township planners got a first look this week at the Grand Traverse Educator Village: 73 affordable apartments on the Oleson Foundation land off US-31.
• It's geared toward TCAPS staff and other school employees: 44 one-bedrooms and 29 two-bedrooms, a dog park, and about four acres of woods kept as open space.
• It's early: concept review only, from Woda Cooper Companies, the developer behind Ruth Park and Annika Place.
➜ TAKE: Teachers who can afford to live in the town they teach in? That's a lesson plan I can get behind.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: which teacher changed your life? Say their name on air.
😂 JOKES: A neighborhood full of teachers. Imagine trying to sneak home late past THAT block. / There's a dog park, so even the dogs will have to raise a paw before speaking.

SCHOOL: IT'S SUBSTITUTE EDUCATORS DAY
• Today is Substitute Educators Day, always the Friday before Thanksgiving, closing out American Education Week.
• National Day Calendar cites more than 500,000 substitute teachers in 2020; some get the call only hours before class.
• Listener question: the best (or wildest) substitute teacher story from your school days.
➜ TAKE: Subs walk into a room of 28 kids they've never met with a lesson plan written on a napkin. Give them a raise and a coffee.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: your best substitute-teacher story. Did your class switch names on the sub?
😂 JOKES: Every class had that kid who told the sub, 'Our teacher always lets us watch a movie.' Every class. / Subs are the bravest people in America. They don't know your name, the Wi-Fi password or where the bathroom is.

mental.title: Mental Health Minute
mental.content:
TWO SIGHS BEFORE THE BIG MOMENT

Big weekend Up North, isn't it? The Stags are headed to Clare, the Snowbirds are headed to Marquette, the tree lights up downtown tonight, and Thanksgiving is barreling at us like a semi on 31. So if your shoulders are up around your ears this morning, that makes sense. Here's one thing that actually helps, and it works sitting right there in your car. Researchers at Stanford had people do something called cyclic sighing for five minutes a day, and after a month those folks felt better and calmer than the group doing regular meditation. It goes like this: breathe in through your nose, then sneak in one more little sip of air on top of it, and then let it all out slow through your mouth, longer than you breathed in. Do that a few times at the red light, before you walk into work, or right before kickoff when your kid runs onto the field. You don't have to fix the whole weekend, you just have to get through the next breath, and then the next one. Try it today and text me how it went at 231-929-4487.

offcharts.content:
SPONSOR (read first): Z93 OFF THE CHARTS is brought to you by Schuss Mountain at Shanty Creek Resort. Trade your screen time for ski time at Northern Michigan's most authentic ski resort, where you can hit the face, take the scenic route through the glades, or send it in the terrain parks. More at shantycreek.com.

THE REMBRANDTS, "I'LL BE THERE FOR YOU" (1995)
• RELEASE: The Friends theme, sent to US pop radio May 23, 1995.
• HOW IT HAPPENED: Producers wanted R.E.M.; when that fell through, they wrote their own theme, with music by Michael Skloff and lyrics by David Crane, Marta Kauffman and Allee Willis. The Rembrandts didn't want to record it, and the handclaps were a last-minute add they now call the best part.
• WHY BILLBOARD MISSED IT: a Nashville DJ looped the TV version into a full song, so the band re-recorded it. At its peak there was no commercial single, so it became the first song to top the Hot 100 Airplay chart (8 weeks) without being on the Hot 100.
• WHERE IT DID CHART: it later reached No. 17 on the Hot 100 as a double A-side with "This House Is Not a Home." No. 1 in Canada for five weeks; UK No. 3 in 1995, top 10 again in 1997.
➜ TAKE: The most famous TV theme ever, and for its biggest summer you couldn't legally put it on the Hot 100. That's the most Friends thing ever: they were on a break.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: Ross or Chandler? And yes, you have to pick.
😂 JOKES: You can't hear this song without clapping four times. It's the law. / The band didn't want to record it. Now it's paid for more than a few lake houses.
